standard.title: Initiate, sustain and extend exchanges
standard.description: initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts related to students' own and others' experiences of the world, adjusting their language in response to others
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts, adjusting register and structuring arguments (AC9LS8C01). They have not yet extended exchanges into fully unfamiliar territory, sustained discussion of others' experiences, or used a full range of discussion management strategies.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students initiate, sustain and extend exchanges in familiar and unfamiliar contexts about their own and others' experiences — using structured argument, discussion management, register adjustment and spontaneous interaction strategies.

nodes.label: Exchanging accounts of experiences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can exchange accounts of their own and others' significant experiences — using narrative, question and response strategies across familiar and unfamiliar contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Share at least one account of a significant experience using narrative structure; ask and respond to questions about another person's experience.
nodes.typical_width: Exchange accounts of significant events, milestones and personal experiences; use narrative techniques to develop accounts; ask follow-up questions about others' experiences; identify common themes across shared accounts.
wider: Exchange accounts with a target language community peer — adapting language and cultural references for the audience
Compare two accounts of the same type of experience from different cultural perspectives — identify what each reveals about the values of each community
nodes.hinge_reason: Exchanging accounts of others' experiences — not only one's own — requires perspective-taking and responsive questioning that is a prerequisite for the discussion and debate work in node 2.

response_modes.reason: Narrative and experiential exchange requires a bank of discourse-level strategies — not only sentence-level structures. Students need varied practice exchanging accounts across different topic areas.

success_criteria: Shares at least one account of a significant experience using narrative structure
Asks and responds to at least two questions about another person's experience

nodes.label: Structuring arguments and managing discussion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can structure arguments, invite contributions and manage discussion flow using a range of discourse strategies.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least two argument-structuring moves and at least two discussion management strategies in a sustained exchange.
nodes.typical_width: Use structured argument language to justify positions; use discussion management strategies for turn-taking, inviting elaboration and requesting clarification; maintain and extend conversations through follow-up questions and connectors; use language for different interactional purposes.
wider: Facilitate a class discussion on a contested topic — managing contributions, summarising positions and steering toward shared understanding
Participate in a discussion where a stated position is challenged — respond to the challenge without abandoning the position unless a compelling reason is given

response_modes.reason: Discussion management strategies develop through varied discussion contexts — different topics, interlocutors and discussion structures each require different management moves.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Genuine discussion management — steering, summarising, maintaining position under challenge — is the oral capability that most distinguishes advanced from intermediate speakers.
success_criteria: Uses at least two argument-structuring moves in a sustained exchange
Uses at least two discussion management strategies effectively

nodes.label: Adjusting language across unfamiliar contexts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can adjust their language across familiar and unfamiliar contexts — using appropriate register, slang or formal language for varied interlocutors and purposes.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate deliberate language adjustment in at least two different contexts — one familiar and one unfamiliar.
nodes.typical_width: Apply appropriate register across formal, informal and digital communication contexts; use contemporary language varieties including abbreviations and colloquial shortening; adjust language in response to interlocutor and context; interact in spontaneous and unscripted situations.
wider: Interact in a fully spontaneous scenario — an unrehearsed situation in an unfamiliar context — applying available language flexibly
Compare language adjustment strategies across two different unfamiliar contexts and explain what signals triggered each adjustment

response_modes.reason: Language adjustment across unfamiliar contexts requires encountering genuinely varied and unpredictable interaction conditions. Rehearsed scenarios do not build the spontaneous adjustment capacity needed.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Spontaneous language adjustment in unfamiliar contexts is the hallmark of genuine communicative competence — the capability that matters most in real-world target language use.
success_criteria: Demonstrates deliberate language adjustment in at least two different contexts
Responds with adequate fluency in at least one unfamiliar or unscripted situation

nodes.label: Sustaining exchanges about complex and topical subjects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can initiate and sustain exchanges about complex and topical subjects — including social issues, global topics and shared experiences — drawing on a full range of interaction strategies.
nodes.minimum_width: Initiate and sustain an exchange on a complex or topical subject for at least six turns using a mix of argument, narrative and discussion management strategies.
nodes.typical_width: Engage in discussion of topical issues, social questions and shared experiences across familiar and unfamiliar subjects; use the full range of interaction strategies developed across prior nodes; sustain extended exchanges with varied interlocutors.
wider: Participate in a sustained exchange on a topic of genuine personal significance — demonstrating that the target language can carry the full weight of the student's thinking
Initiate and maintain a target language exchange with a community member on a topic of mutual interest — adapting spontaneously to the interlocutor's responses

response_modes.reason: Extended exchanges on complex subjects integrate all prior interaction capabilities — narrative, argument, management and adjustment — in a sustained communicative performance.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Sustaining exchanges on topics of genuine personal significance is where the target language becomes a fully functional communicative tool — not only a school subject.
success_criteria: Initiates and sustains an exchange on a complex or topical subject for at least six turns
Uses a mix of at least three different interaction strategies across the exchange
